No lesson prose, bank, key truth or migration is written yet.
plan.thesis: An electrofacies is a group of depth samples whose logs look alike, and it is worth something only when it is checked against the rock. Associate owns GROUPING LOGS INTO ELECTROFACIES (logs as features, distance and why a raw distance is ruled by GR, standard and min-max scaling, principal components from the correlation matrix, k-means with seeded k-means++ and several starts, centres in log units, new rows at the nearest centre, the published iris check), Professional owns JUDGING GROUPS AGAINST CORE (the elbow, the silhouette, agglomerative Ward, complete and average linkage with the linkage matrix and its cut, matching clusters to core facies one to one and by majority, the adjusted Rand index), Expert owns PREDICTING FACIES AND THE ENGINE'S OWN RULES (k nearest neighbours with the scaler fitted on the training rows and its tie rules, the CART tree, its exact tie-break and importances, the uncored wells predicted and written back, boundaries rule by rule, the tie band, the sign rule, the row caps, conventions that are choices). Each capstone grades only its own tier's question.

tiers.beginner: Associate: m01 what electrofacies are (logs as a signature of rock, core facies and electrofacies, the Ekene facies wells, rows features and distance, refusals), m02 scaling before distance, m03 principal components, m04 k-means, m05 reading clusters (centres in log units, cluster numbers are names, new rows, covariance against correlation), m06 one field clustered end to end (with Fisher's iris as the published check). Digest sections 1 to 13, and section 28.
tiers.intermediate: Professional: m01 choosing k with the elbow, m02 the silhouette, m03 agglomerative clustering, m04 matching clusters to core facies, m05 the adjusted Rand index, m06 electrofacies against core end to end. Digest sections 14 to 20. Precision, recall and F1 of a mapped facies are D2's ratios, read with a pointer and never re-derived.
tiers.advanced: Expert: m01 k nearest neighbours, m02 classification trees, m03 ties and exact comparisons, m04 predicting uncored wells, m05 boundaries, bands and caps, m06 reading the engine honestly. Digest sections 21 to 27.

plan.tierScopeDecisions: Refined from the lead's split: the sign convention of a PCA component is NAMED in Associate (section 7 prints the basis) and its banded tie rule is Expert (section 26); the refusals are owned across all three tiers; the uncalibrated gamma ray tool and the withheld facies belong to Expert m04 only; Fisher's iris is Associate (the published PCA ratio and the k-means inertia) while its tied one-leaf tree is an Expert golden. Nothing in a lower tier needs a higher tier's section.
plan.stage: FOUNDATION. run_gates.py expects numsweep_facies.mjs and lengths.py to refuse on the 78 stubs for their stated stub reasons; D3_STAGE=lessons flips both to must-pass.

history.position: THIS COURSE TEACHES NO REPAIR HISTORY. The engine's review changes (the banded ties, the robust sign rule, the kNN pair cap) landed before its merge and before any lesson was written; they are provenance. The digest describes the engine as it is.

scopeSeams.splits, cross-validation and scores: OWNED BY D2 mlcore (groupSplit, groupKFold, leakage, regression metrics, precision, recall, F1 and their averages). D3 states which cored well is held out and reads the classification report of a mapped or predicted facies with a pointer; it never re-derives a ratio.
scopeSeams.log conditioning and outliers: OWNED BY D1 dataqc. D3 takes clean logs, refuses a missing value by name, and names gamma ray normalisation between wells as a conditioning step it does not do.
scopeSeams.petrophysical interpretation: OWNED BY the petrophysics course (porosity, saturation, net pay). A facies here is a label on a row.

namingCollisions.cluster: a group the engine made without core, numbered from 0; the number is a name. Section 28.
namingCollisions.facies: a core facies, or one predicted from core and called predicted; an electrofacies takes a facies name only after matching. Section 28.
namingCollisions.standard deviation: names its divisor: the clustering scaler's population SD against the correlation PCA's sample SD. Sections 5, 6, 28.
namingCollisions.distance: Euclidean on the scaled logs unless raw is said. Section 28.
namingCollisions.accuracy: names its rows: training, a held-out cored well, or the withheld facies of the synthetic field. Section 28.
namingCollisions.machine learning: a method named by what it is; no AI claim. Gated by gate_vocabulary.py.

openItems.ENGINE FINDING E1 (repair first): The constant-log refusal cluster.js inherits from ml.js calls the rows the scaler was fitted on 'training rows' when pca (correlation), kmeans, silhouette, elbow and agglomerative refuse: 'X.CALI has zero variance on the 30 training rows (every value is 8.5): standardising would divide by zero, so drop the feature or fit on rows where it varies'. Clustering and PCA have no training rows; the digest (section 3) states the wording as it is. Reported to the lead for an engines PR; the foundation re-cuts after it.
